assessment.summary: Buyer says the $95 ceramic table lamp arrived with a crack down one side and asks for a refund or replacement. The shop packed fragile ceramic in a single box without double-boxing, so I recommend offering a full $95 refund (no return needed) after checking the existing $91.47 pending refund.
assessment.buyer_claim: The lamp base arrived cracked down one side and is unsafe to use, and the buyer wants a replacement lamp or a refund.

No photo of the crack has been submitted by the buyer; the evidence list has only the buyer's text.
Allowed responses on this dispute: accept (partial refund, refund with return, refund) or make an offer (refund, refund with return). A replacement is not an offer type here.
Shop packing note: the item was packed in a single box without double-boxing.
Store policy: items damaged in transit are replaced or refunded on receipt of a photo, and return shipping is on the seller when the item arrived damaged.
USPS tracking 9400111202061111222233 is attached to the capture. The shop record shows delivery on 2026-10-28 with a delivery photo flagged as on file.
The shop record's delivery time (15:08:26) is only 25 seconds after its ship time (15:08:01). PayPal's tracker still shows SHIPPED with no delivered event, so the delivery record needs checking.
A refund 1FA210790C4770820 for $91.47 is already PENDING on the capture, with a matching $91.47 HOLD_PLACED debit. This must be reconciled before any new refund is sent.
Seller protection on the capture is eligible only for ITEM_NOT_RECEIVED and UNAUTHORIZED_TRANSACTION. This dispute is a not-as-described claim, so protection may not apply.

Buyer history: 2 other orders totaling $201 and 1 prior dispute. The first order timestamp is one minute before this disputed order.

Carrier scan history for USPS 9400111202061111222233 confirming delivery and its timestamp; PayPal still shows SHIPPED
The delivery photo itself (the shop record only flags that one exists)
Packing details or photos showing how the lamp was padded
Origin of the pending $91.47 refund 1FA210790C4770820: was it initiated by the shop, and for what
Details of the buyer's prior dispute
assessment.win_probability_reasoning: Fighting is weak. The shop packed fragile ceramic in a single box without double-boxing, and the buyer says the box looked fine from outside, which points to inadequate protection in transit. Delivery is confirmed by USPS and the shop record, but the timestamps are inconsistent and the PayPal tracker still shows SHIPPED. The buyer has not supplied a photo, which helps the seller somewhat, but the store's own policy refunds transit damage. A reviewer would likely side with the buyer.
assessment.action_reasoning: The economics tool says fighting is cheaper by about $3 in expectation (break-even win probability 0.173 versus my 0.2). I am overriding that: the packing shortfall is the shop's, the store policy refunds transit damage, and a fight risks a $15 fee plus a worse relationship with a buyer who has a broken item. A full $95 refund offer lets the buyer accept without returning the lamp. Before sending, confirm whether the existing $91.47 pending refund was shop-initiated. If it was for this dispute, the balance to offer is $3.53 and the offer amount should be adjusted to avoid over-refunding. A replacement is not an offer type on this dispute, so a replacement would have to be arranged separately.
assessment.buyer_message: Hi John, I'm sorry your sage ceramic table lamp arrived cracked. It was shipped in a single box without extra protection, and it should have been packed better for the trip. I've offered a full refund of $95.00 for the lamp through the dispute. You don't need to send the lamp back. If you're able, a photo of the crack would help us improve our packing, but it isn't required. Under our policy, refunds go to your original PayPal payment within 3 business days of approval.
risk_flags: A $91.47 refund (1FA210790C4770820) is already PENDING on the capture with a matching hold debit. Confirm its origin before sending the offer, to avoid refunding twice.
The economics tool favored fighting by about $3. This recommendation overrides that on fairness and the packing fault. Say so if you decide otherwise.
Seller protection on the capture covers ITEM_NOT_RECEIVED and UNAUTHORIZED_TRANSACTION only, not not-as-described claims.
The shop's delivery timestamp (25 seconds after ship time) conflicts with PayPal's tracker, which still shows SHIPPED. Check the carrier record before relying on delivery as evidence.
The buyer's first order is timestamped one minute before this disputed order. Check the account and the prior dispute before any future orders from this buyer.
Replacement is not a valid make-offer type on this dispute. The buyer's replacement request can only be met through a separate message and arrangement.
The store policy asks for a photo before a transit-damage refund. The offer does not require one, so the seller is choosing to waive that step.

assessment.summary: The buyer says the $189 merino throw never arrived. The shop record claims delivery and a signature, but PayPal tracking shows only SHIPPED and the shop's timestamps are implausible, so I recommend accepting the refund rather than fighting.
assessment.buyer_claim: The buyer says the merino wool throw (oat, $189.00) never arrived and asks for a full refund.

key_facts.fact: The buyer opened the dispute at 15:15:33 on 2026-10-28, about 15 minutes after the 15:00:14 capture, claiming the item never arrived.
The PayPal tracker for USPS 9400179320009232893696 has status SHIPPED, and no carrier delivery confirmation is on file.
The shop record shows shipped at 15:08:12 and delivered at 15:08:24 on 2026-10-28, signed for by JOHN DOE.
The shop's delivered timestamp is 12 seconds after its shipped timestamp, which is not plausible for a USPS parcel to Geneva, so the record is unreliable as delivery proof.
The order ships to Rue de Bourgogne 5, Geneva 1211, CH, which matches the PayPal order and the payer's country.
Store policy requires signature confirmation for orders over $150, and this $189 order is over that threshold, so a signature is required proof.
The buyer has 2 prior disputes and 2 other orders totaling $107, but their first-order timestamp (15:01:01 on the same day) does not fit that history.
The PayPal payment record lists a PENDING refund of $182.27 on the capture.
The seller has already sent PayPal supporting information at 15:42:16 that cites the shop-record delivery and signature as fact.

missing_evidence: USPS carrier scan for 9400179320009232893696 showing delivery to Geneva and the signature. This is the only item that would change the outcome.
An explanation or corrected fulfillment record for the 15:08:12 shipped and 15:08:24 delivered timestamps.
Proof of postage or label showing the actual ship date and the international service used.
Any delivery photo or packing photo. None is on file.
Confirmation of what the pending $182.27 refund on the capture is (a hold versus a real refund) before any payout is triggered.
assessment.win_probability_reasoning: About 10%. PayPal tracking shows only SHIPPED with no carrier delivery confirmation. The signature exists only in the shop record, and that record's delivery time is 12 seconds after shipment, which a reviewer would reject. The Geneva address match and the signature policy help only slightly. The code cap may lower this further.
assessment.action_reasoning: Fight is cheaper on paper, but only by about $1.40 at a 10% win chance (break-even about 9.3%). The difference only reaches about $22 if the win chance is 20%, which the evidence does not support. That small gap is outweighed by fairness and by evidence integrity: fighting would mean asking PayPal to accept a delivery and signature from a shop record whose timestamps cannot be right and which PayPal's own tracking does not confirm. Accepting closes the dispute and refunds $189.00 automatically, and the buyer is treated fairly. Before accepting, check USPS 9400179320009232893696 directly. If the carrier shows delivered with a signature, switch to FIGHT, because the evidence would then be strong. Also confirm the pending $182.27 refund so the buyer is not refunded twice.

We have not been able to confirm delivery on USPS tracking 9400179320009232893696, so we are accepting your claim. The full $189.00 will be returned to your original PayPal payment method. We're sorry the throw didn't reach you, and we hope to see you again at Lumen & Loom.

assessment.summary: Buyer says a $12.00 tealight order never arrived. The shop shipped it by Royal Mail with no tracking, so there is no delivery proof; I recommend accepting the claim and refunding the buyer in full.
assessment.buyer_claim: The buyer says they never received their $12.00 beeswax tealights (6 pack), two weeks after purchase, and is disputing it as merchandise not received.

key_facts.fact: Dispute reason is MERCHANDISE_OR_SERVICE_NOT_RECEIVED for $12.00 on capture 28A73920SJ282125Y; buyer message says 'Never got my tealights, it's been two weeks.'
No tracking records are attached to the PayPal transaction; the tracking list is empty.
Shop record notes say the order was 'Sent without tracking to keep shipping cheap.' Carrier is listed as Royal Mail, shipped 2026-10-28 at 15:05 UTC.
Evidence checklist: tracking on the PayPal transaction is missing, and there is no carrier delivery scan on file.
Store policy says orders ship within 2 business days with tracking. The untracked shipment does not follow this policy.
Ship-to address on the PayPal order and the shop record both point to Geneva, CH, the same address as the payer, so the address matches the payment.
Dispute allows full refund of $12.00. The PayPal fund movement shows an $11.29 HOLD_PLACED debit, and refund 8R3120707W3311110 for $11.29 is PENDING.
Estimated expected cost of fighting is $29.65 (including the $15 dispute fee if lost) versus $12.00 to accept. Break-even win probability is 70.4%.
Buyer history shows 2 other orders, $284.00 total spent, and 2 prior disputes.
Seller response is due 2026-11-17. The merchant has not been contacted yet.

missing_evidence: Carrier proof of delivery or delivery scan from Royal Mail. None exists because no tracking number was recorded.
Any proof of posting (postage receipt or dispatch record) with a tracking or reference number. Nothing on file shows the parcel was actually sent via a traceable route.
Confirmation of whether the pending $11.29 refund (8R3120707W3311110) was created by the shop or by PayPal's hold, and whether it conflicts with a full $12.00 refund.
assessment.win_probability_reasoning: The shop has no tracking, no delivery scan and no signature, and its own records say the parcel was sent untracked to save on shipping. Those facts contradict the shop's stated policy. A PayPal reviewer would side with the buyer on item-not-received, so fighting is very unlikely to succeed.
assessment.action_reasoning: Accepting costs $12.00 (the sale amount), while fighting has an expected cost of about $29.65 and needs a 70% win chance to break even. The shop can't prove delivery and the shipment broke its own tracking policy, so the claim is fair and fighting would just add the $15 dispute fee. Accepting also protects the relationship: the buyer gets their money back quickly. The shop should first confirm the pending $11.29 refund so the buyer isn't refunded twice or left with a mismatch.
assessment.buyer_message: Hello John, thank you for letting us know your tealights haven't arrived, and I'm sorry for the wait. Your parcel was sent by Royal Mail to Geneva without tracking, so we can't confirm delivery on our side. We're refunding your $12.00 in full to your original PayPal payment. Our policy is to ship with tracking, and we are fixing that for future orders. We hope to make candles for you again soon.
